meta.title: Bardejov UNESCO — Town Hall Square, St Giles and spa
meta.description: Visit UNESCO Bardejov: Town Hall Square, the basilica of St Giles, the town walls, the Jewish suburb and Bardejov Spa. A guide to the free royal town in Šariš, Slovakia.
meta.keywords: Bardejov, UNESCO Bardejov, Town Hall Square, St Giles basilica, Bardejov Spa, Šariš, free royal town, Bardejov walls, Jewish suburb, Slovakia, Prešov
meta.imageAlt: Town Hall Square in Bardejov, a UNESCO site, at dusk

ui.preUnesco: World Heritage 2000 · St Giles’ basilica · town square
ui.heroSub: Enter Slovakia’s most Gothic town by quiet thresholds, where guild, faith and walls still hold the square together.
ui.chip0p: A square that opens deeper paths into the town’s core.
ui.chip1p: A belt of ramparts, bastions and gates the town still holds.
ui.chip2p: Hands, altars and memory that shape the reverence.
ui.chip3p: Springs that wake when the day falls quiet.
ui.peekAria: Dusk tour of the square, 32 seconds
ui.gateH: Cat-head cobbles, red gables, one tower over all.
ui.gateLead: Bardejov begins where Šariš narrows into a rectangle: 260 by 80 metres of paving, the town hall in the middle, the basilica to the north, forty-six burgher houses with narrow Gothic plots on three sides.
ui.gateBody: This square was a market on the road between the Black Sea and the Baltic. More than fifty guilds kept the town alive here. In 1376 it became a free royal town. In 2000 UNESCO listed it as one of the most complete fortified medieval layouts in Central Europe — together with the Jewish suburb.
ui.lesH: Five chapters. Eight centuries. One square.
ui.lesIntro: Each chapter is a walk, not a lecture. You come to a gate, climb a tower, sit by a spring and leave with one thing worth keeping.
ui.les0p: A three-aisled Gothic church of the 15th century and eleven unique winged altars that stayed in their places.
ui.les0b: The tower stands 72 metres. Inside remain eleven late-Gothic winged altars from 1440–1520 — most on their original sites, each bound to a guild. The neo-Gothic high altar of 1878 is the tallest in Slovakia.
ui.les0how: Northern edge of Town Hall Square. Eight minutes from the bus station along Dlhý rad, then straight onto the paving.
ui.les0hrs: Mon–Fri 10:00–16:00 · Sat 10:00–15:00 · Sun 11:30–14:30. The tower and its Šariš view are included with interior entry.
ui.les1p: 1505: Gothic cellar, Renaissance storey. Today the Šariš Museum, one of the oldest in Slovakia.
ui.les1b: The first building in Hungary that served the town, not the church or the walls. Today it holds the exhibition Free Royal Town of Bardejov. A Gothic hall in the cellar; guild chests and the town arms upstairs.
ui.les1how: Centre of the square, Radničné námestie 48. The square is pedestrian — leave the car by the walls.
ui.les1hrs: Tue–Sun, Monday closed. May–Sep 8:30–16:30 (lunch 12:30–13:00). Oct–Apr until 16:00.
ui.les2p: A trade road between Hungary and Poland. The ius gladii of 1365, and a free royal town eleven years later.
ui.les2b: Weavers, potters, tailors, carpenters, sievemakers, masons. Each guild had an altar in the basilica and a plot on the square. The town lived off the road between the Black Sea and the Baltic — and off the hands that served that road.
ui.les2how: Read the guild gables on the southern and eastern fronts of the square. Walk the outer circuit of wall and bastions, about 1.2 km.
ui.les2hrs: The walls are freely accessible. Some bastions seasonally, according to TIK Bardejov.
ui.les3p: Synagogue, mikveh and beth hamidrash from the 18th century — the other half of the UNESCO listing, not a footnote.
ui.les3b: Beyond the southern walls a complete Jewish settlement grew in the 18th century: synagogue, ritual bath, school. UNESCO listed it with the square because without it the portrait of the town would lie.
ui.les3how: From the square through the southern gate, then Domašínska to the synagogue. Five minutes on foot, level ground.
ui.les3hrs: Exterior always. Synagogue interior via TIK or by appointment — check before you travel.
ui.les4p: Mineral springs in the valley under Busov. Sissi, Tsar Alexander I and Marie Louise, Napoleon’s wife.
ui.les4b: Five kilometres north, in the valley under Busov. Eight springs, a colonnade, Slovakia’s oldest open-air museum. People came here to be silent once the square had finished speaking.
ui.les4how: Buses 1, 2 and 5 from Slovenská-stanica to Bardejovské Kúpele, parkovisko. About 15 minutes. On foot along the cycle path about 70 minutes.
ui.les4hrs: Park and colonnade free. Springs year-round. Cars enter the grounds only exceptionally — park by the bus stop.
ui.annH: A tape the town still holds.
ui.ann1241: After the Tatar invasion a settlement remains in Šariš, from which the town will grow.
ui.ann1365: The right of the sword. Bardejov may judge — and defend itself — as a royal body.
ui.ann1376: Free royal town. The square ceases to be a market and becomes a plan.
ui.ann1505: The town hall into the centre. Gothic below, Renaissance above — the town builds itself a mirror.
ui.ann18c: Beyond the southern walls: synagogue, mikveh, beth hamidrash. The other half of a later listing.
ui.ann2000: Listing 973. One of the most complete fortified medieval layouts in Central Europe.
ui.gldLead: Each guild had a plot on the square and a wing in the basilica. The shield is a pact between work and faith.
ui.gldHint: Touch the arms. The guild opens a wing in the basilica.
ui.altH: Wings the guild left in place.
ui.altHint: Wheel or drag to pass all eleven wings.
ui.altCred: Altar photographs: Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0
ui.subH: Not a suburb. The other half of the listing.
ui.subLead: Beyond the southern walls a complete settlement remains: synagogue, mikveh, beth hamidrash. UNESCO listed it in 2000 with the square — proof that a medieval town also had a later, equally fragile courtyard.
ui.subBody: The 18th-century synagogue still holds polychromy on its vault. The mikveh lies below street level. The beth hamidrash, the house of study, stood close beside. This is not an annex to the Gothic. It is a memory without which Bardejov would lie about itself.
ui.subSynP: A Baroque hall, a painted ceiling, a women’s gallery. The heart of the suburb.
ui.subMikP: A ritual bath below the street. Water that clears the calendar.
ui.subMidP: A house of learning by the synagogue. The third point without which the settlement is incomplete.
ui.walkH: One paving. Three lengths of day.
ui.practParkD: The square is pedestrian. Cars by the walls and at intercept parks along the ramparts.
ui.practMhdD: Lines 1, 2, 5 · stop Bardejovské Kúpele, parkovisko · about 15 min from Slovenská.
ui.finP: The gate does not close behind you. When Šariš falls quiet, the same road remains from the square to the spring — and never the same light.
ui.footBlurb: A dusk walk through UNESCO Bardejov. A live square, walls, altars, suburb and the springs of Šariš.
ui.err404p: The threshold you want is not in these walls. The square is one step back — paving, tower and dusk still stand.
ui.err500p: The walk has stopped. Try the courtyard once more, or return to the paving while the stone still remembers.

voice.top: You enter Bardejov. Here the stone still remembers kings. Slovakia’s most Gothic town opens through quiet thresholds, where guild, faith and ramparts hold the square together. Dusk over Šariš. Unesco since the year two thousand.
voice.gate: Town Hall Square. Two hundred and sixty metres by eighty. Cat-head cobbles underfoot, the town hall in the centre, the basilica of Saint Giles to the north. On three sides, forty-six burgher houses on narrow Gothic plots. This square was a market on the road between the Black Sea and the Baltic. More than fifty guilds kept the town alive here. In thirteen seventy-six it became a free royal town. In two thousand Unesco listed it as one of the most complete fortified medieval plans in Central Europe.
voice.pathways: The walls still hold the town. A belt of ramparts, bastions and gates that takes half an hour to walk. The outer circuit is about one kilometre two hundred metres. The Thick Bastion looks out over Šariš. Some bastions open in season; the wall itself is free to walk. This is not decoration. It is a belt the town still holds.
voice.lessons: Five chapters. Eight centuries. One square. The basilica of Saint Giles, with eleven winged altars and a tower of seventy-two metres. The town hall of fifteen oh five: Gothic cellar, Renaissance storey, today the Šariš Museum. Fifty guilds, each with a plot on the square and a wing in the basilica. The Jewish suburb beyond the southern walls. And the spa in the valley under Busov, five kilometres north. Each chapter is a walk, not a lecture.
voice.suburb: Beyond the southern walls remains the Jewish suburb. Synagogue, mikveh and beth hamidrash from the eighteenth century. Unesco listed it with the square in two thousand, because without it the picture of the town would lie. The synagogue still holds polychromy on its vault. The mikveh lies below street level. The house of study stood next door. This is not a footnote to the Gothic. It is the other half of the inscription.
voice.walk: Choose the length of the day. Two hours: the square, the basilica, the eastern walls. Half a day adds the rampart circuit and the Jewish suburb. A full day leads from the cobbles to the spring at Bardejov Spa. The square is pedestrian. Leave the car by the walls.
voice.eternity: When Šariš falls quiet, the road from the square to the spring remains. Bardejov Spa lies five kilometres north, in the valley under Busov. Eight springs, a colonnade, the oldest open-air museum in Slovakia. People came here to be silent once the square had spoken. The gate does not close behind you. It is never the same light.

tour.title: Threshold of the square
tour.k: Cat-head cobbles. Red gables. One tower.

tour.title: St Giles
tour.k: Eleven altars. A tower of seventy-two metres.

tour.title: Walls
tour.k: A belt of ramparts and bastions the town still holds.

2h: Paving, 46 houses, axis and tower. 20 min.
Altars and the view from 72 m. 40 min.
Bastion and rampart above Šariš. 25 min.
full: Southern gate to the synagogue. 1.5 h.

1241.title: After the invasion
1241.lead: The Tatar invasion leaves in Šariš a settlement from which the town will grow.
1241.body: Bardejov is not born of peace. It is born of what remains when the steppe leaves and the stone stays.
1241.how: You read this layer in the town-hall museum and in the plan of the square.

1365.title: Right of the sword
1365.lead: Bardejov may judge and defend itself as a royal body.
1365.body: Ius gladii is the threshold before a free town. Eleven years later comes the title the square still wears.

1376.title: Free royal town
1376.lead: The square ceases to be only a market and becomes a plan.
1376.body: Forty-six plots, walls, guild. Since then Bardejov is measured by a rectangle 260 × 80 metres.
1376.how: Step onto the paving. The plan is underfoot.

1505.title: Town hall to the centre
1505.lead: Gothic below, Renaissance above. The town builds itself a mirror.
1505.body: A building that serves neither altar nor bastion, but the commune. It still stands on the axis of the square.

2000.title: Listing 973
2000.lead: One of the most complete fortified medieval layouts in Central Europe.
2000.body: The listing holds the square and the Jewish suburb. Not decoration — a plan you can still walk.
2000.how: Begin on the square; end at the synagogue or at the spa.

square.title: Town Hall Square
square.lead: Two hundred and sixty by eighty metres of paving. The town hall in the middle, the tower to the north, forty-six burgher gables on three sides.
square.body: This square was a market on the road between the Black Sea and the Baltic. In 1376 it became a free royal town. UNESCO listed it in 2000 as one of the most complete fortified layouts in Central Europe.
square.how: Town centre. Eight minutes from the bus station along Dlhý rad. The square is pedestrian.

hall.title: Town Hall
hall.lead: Gothic cellar, Renaissance storey. The first building in Hungary that served the town, not the church or the walls.
hall.body: Today the Šariš Museum — the exhibition Free Royal Town of Bardejov. Guild chests, the arms, and a hall where debate can still be heard.
hall.how: Centre of the square, Radničné námestie 48. Leave the car by the walls.

basilica.title: Basilica of St Giles
basilica.lead: Three-aisled Gothic and eleven winged altars that stayed in their places. The tower stands 72 metres.
basilica.body: Each altar bound a guild. The neo-Gothic high altar of 1878 is the tallest in Slovakia. From the tower Šariš reads like an open book.
basilica.how: Northern edge of the square. Enter from the paving; the tower by stairs.

walls.title: Walls and the Thick Bastion
walls.lead: A belt of ramparts, gates and bastions the town still holds. The circuit around the core is about 1.2 kilometres.
walls.body: The Thick Bastion is the largest link. From the wall-walk you see why the square fitted inside and the suburb stayed beyond the wall.
walls.how: The eastern and southern stretches are the most legible. Enter at the bastions; the ground is gentle.

synagogue.title: Synagogue
synagogue.lead: A Baroque hall with a painted vault. The heart of the Jewish suburb UNESCO listed with the square.
synagogue.body: Without this building the listing would lie. The settlement beyond the southern walls is not an annex to the Gothic — it is the other half of the town.
synagogue.how: From the square through the southern gate, Domašínska to the synagogue. Five minutes on foot.

mikve.title: Mikveh
mikve.lead: A ritual bath below street level. Water that holds the community’s calendar.
mikve.body: The mikveh belongs to the synagogue as the tower belongs to the basilica: without it the suburb would be a façade.
mikve.how: Beside the synagogue, below ground. Entry by arrangement through TIK.

midrash.title: Beth hamidrash
midrash.lead: A house of learning by the synagogue. The third point without which the settlement is incomplete.
midrash.body: The study house stood in a tight courtyard. UNESCO reads the suburb as a set, not as a single monument.
midrash.how: Beside the synagogue, south of the walls. Exterior freely.

spa.title: Bardejov Spa
spa.lead: Five kilometres north, a valley under Busov. Sissi, Tsar Alexander I, Marie Louise.
spa.body: Eight mineral springs, a colonnade and Slovakia’s oldest open-air museum. People came here to be silent once the square had finished speaking.
spa.how: Buses 1, 2 and 5 from Slovenská to Bardejovské Kúpele, parkovisko. About 15 min.

weavers.title: Weavers
weavers.lead: The guild that held the Nativity altar — the rarest wings in the basilica.
weavers.body: Cloth went north from the square, into Poland. The weavers paid for the altar; the altar held their name.
weavers.how: Look for the weavers’ gables on the southern row of burgher houses.

potters.title: Potters
potters.lead: Altar of St Erasmus and St Nicholas. Clay, fire, and the saints of roads.
potters.body: The potters’ guild fed market and household. Their wings stayed in the nave, not in a museum.
potters.how: Eastern front of the square, narrow Gothic plots.

tailors.title: Tailors
tailors.lead: Altar of St Elizabeth of Hungary. The town was sewn together with a needle as much as with walls.
tailors.body: The tailors served the trade road: cloth from Hungary, cut from Kraków.
tailors.how: The town hall keeps the guild chests in the museum.

carpenters.title: Carpenters
carpenters.lead: Vir Dolorum — Man of Sorrows. Wood that carries stone.
carpenters.body: Without the carpenters the tower, the roof and the town hall would have stayed a drawing. Their altar dates from 1500–1510.
carpenters.how: The roofs of hall and basilica are their signature, even if you cannot see it from the paving.

masons.title: Masons and stonecutters
masons.lead: A Pietà in stone. The guild that quite literally built the town.
masons.body: The masons’ altar holds one of the nave’s most precious sculptures — a stone Pietà.
masons.how: The walls are their open workshop. Circuit 1.2 km.

furriers.title: Furriers
furriers.lead: Fur went north before the word UNESCO. A guild of quiet and winter.
furriers.body: Bardejov stood on a merchant road. The furriers bound Šariš to Poland more tightly than the walls.
furriers.how: Northern side of the square, in the basilica’s shadow.

gold.title: Goldsmiths
gold.lead: Chalice, seal, town arms. The guild that gave the town sheen on paper and on the altar.
gold.body: Goldsmiths’ work is in the town-hall museum and in the basilica’s liturgical objects.

sieves.title: Sievemakers
sieves.lead: Altar of St Apollonia. A guild of sieves, flour and a quiet market.
sieves.body: The sievemakers held one of the smaller but complete winged altars — proof a guild need not be rich, only bound.
sieves.how: Basilica, side aisle. Altar of Apollonia.

farmers.title: Farmers
farmers.lead: Altar of the Holy Cross. The guild that fed the town while the craft guilds sewed it.
farmers.body: The farmers’ altar of 1480–1490. Fields beyond the walls, a cross in the nave.
farmers.how: Basilica of St Giles, side altar of the Cross.

andrew.title: Altar of St Andrew
andrew.lead: One of the oldest winged altars in the nave.
andrew.body: Andrew as apostle of roads sits well with a town that lived by the road. The wings still stand on their original site.
andrew.how: Basilica of St Giles, enter from the square.

barbara.title: Altar of St Barbara
barbara.lead: Patron of towers and lightning — in a town whose tower stands 72 metres.
barbara.body: Barbara holds a Gothic tower in her hand. Bardejov had her in stone and in wood.
barbara.how: Side aisle, left of the entrance.

elisabeth.title: Altar of St Elizabeth of Hungary
elisabeth.lead: The tailors’ wings. Cloth and mercy in one shrine.
elisabeth.body: Elizabeth, patron of the poor, and the tailors’ guild — a pact between needle and altar.

ann.title: Altar of the Virgin / St Anne
ann.lead: Marian wings, once known as the altar of St Anne.
ann.body: One of two Marian altars. Quieter, older, still in its place.

mager.title: Altar of Veronica Mager
mager.lead: The second Marian altar, bound to a burgher’s gift.
mager.body: The donor’s name stayed on the wings. The town signed itself this way too — not only by guild.

cross.title: Altar of the Holy Cross
cross.lead: The farmers’ altar. At the centre of the predella a Veraicon — the face of Christ.
cross.body: A Crucifixion from the late 15th century. The field beyond the walls has its cross in the nave.
cross.how: Presbytery / side altar of the Cross.

pieta.title: Altar of the Pietà
pieta.lead: The masons’ and stonecutters’ altar. A stone Pietà in the shrine.
pieta.body: One of the basilica’s most precious sculptures. The guild of stone left stone in the nave, not wood.

apollonia.title: Altar of St Apollonia
apollonia.lead: The sievemakers’ altar. A small guild, complete wings.
apollonia.body: Apollonia as patron of quiet crafts. Proof an altar need not be rich, only promised.

nativity.title: Altar of the Nativity
nativity.lead: The finest and most precious wings in the church. The weavers’ guild.
nativity.body: The Nativity of 1480–1490 is among the rarest late-Gothic altars in Slovakia. It stayed in place.
nativity.how: Nave, the weavers’ altar — do not miss it.

erasmus.title: Altar of St Erasmus and St Nicholas
erasmus.lead: The potters’ altar. Two saints, one clay.
erasmus.body: Erasmus and Nicholas as protectors of roads and sailors — in a town that had no sea, only the road toward it.

sorrows.title: Altar of the Man of Sorrows
sorrows.lead: The carpenters’ altar. Wood carries both grief and the roof.
sorrows.body: Vir Dolorum from the turn of the century. The carpenters’ guild gave the nave a figure to walk around slowly.

18c.title: Suburb beyond the wall
18c.lead: Synagogue, mikveh, beth hamidrash. The other half of a later listing.
18c.body: The 18th century added to the Gothic core a settlement without which UNESCO in 2000 would have lied.
